        This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
🐆 Five things to know Friday The Jaguars demolished the shorthanded Ravens. Baltimore's outlook was bleak heading into Week 9, and the result was even more lopsided than expected. With Lamar Jackson on injured reserve and Tyler Huntley out for the season, the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens entered the contest as 10-point underdogs. The undrafted rookie led an offense that found the end zone only in garbage time in a 33-10 drubbing. Help is on the way with Jacoby Brissett poised to arrive over the weekend, but will it be too little, too late? Meanwhile, Jacksonville is taking care of business as a lopsided favorite and has solidified its position as a Super Bowl contender.Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings in Week 9. A hamstring strain will sideline Kyler Murray for the "Monday Night Football" clash with the Bills, prompting a quarterback change that could last beyond just one game. Although it is a somewhat precautionary move, Murray had been struggling when healthy, so Wentz may have a chance to take the job and run with it. The Vikings need a more productive offense to capitalize on their league-best defense, and this swap might just provide that. It could also be a boon to the fantasy football value of Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison.Bronny James' NBA future is uncertain. The Lakers assigned James and rookie Cameron Carr to the G League, and for the former, this marks the third consecutive year in which he has spent time away from the NBA roster. James' contract is guaranteed through the end of the season but not beyond that, so there is a chance the Lakers could move on if he does not earn his way back into the rotation. Since LeBron James is no longer with the franchise, there is even less incentive to keep his son around beyond this year.LIV Golf will cease operations. That's a wrap on the league, which finds itself in a financial bind with its new investor walking back its $300 million pledge. BC Partners pulled its support due to the underwhelming volume and caliber of players committed to "LIV Golf 2.0." The shutdown process will begin next week. Once a disruptive force in the golf world and a thorn in the side of the PGA Tour, the league previously backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is no longer viable and will see its biggest stars -- Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau chief among them -- search for new opportunities. It is unclear where they will land.Cristiano Ronaldo has played his final match for Portugal. One of the greatest soccer superstars of all time announced his retirement from the national team, ending a legendary era that featured a Euro 2016 title and two UEFA Nations League championships. Ronaldo's exit from international competition comes on the heels of a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus that resulted in a 30-day suspension. While it was a bumpy conclusion to his national team career, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner will be remembered for his trophies, the 146 goals he scored in a Portuguese jersey and the transcendent stardom that made him, at his peak, the most famous athlete in the world. 💭 Do not miss this: Biggest MLB offseason questions 
                                                                    Adam Eargle, CBS Sports Design
                                                            Barring any miraculous surprises, we're destined for a dramatic baseball offseason filled with questions about the future of the sport. It is basically a foregone conclusion that MLB will face a work stoppage at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. The lockout is coming. The real uncertainty surrounds how long it will last. That is the absolute biggest question that we hope will be answered sooner rather than later. Collective bargaining negotiations will likely bring fundamental changes to the Major Leagues, whether it's the landmark institution of a salary cap, a shorter regular season, or numerous other proposed moves. Surely, we will get tired of CBA talk before long. So what about the actual baseball? We have questions about free agency and the trade market, too, as Hot Stove season heats up. Our Dayn Perry explained why one of the weakest free agent classes in modern history could still go down as a groundbreaking one. 
Perry: "Tarik Skubal, who turns 30 on Nov. 20, remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and he's going to be paid like it. The expectation is that he'll wind up signing the largest pitcher contract in MLB history and perhaps also fetch the highest-ever annual salary for a pitcher. It's not out of the question that Skubal's next contract could approach or even surpass $400 million in total value." ☑️ College football Week 10 picks 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Get ready for the biggest weekend of the college football season to date. Five ranked matchups. Two top-10 showdowns. CFP implications galore. Now that the selection committee has weighed in with its first rankings of the year, we know which games it will have its eyes on the closest and how those marquee contests will reshape the resumes of the teams involved. There is not a bigger game on the slate than No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame. Although the Malachi Toney injury shook up the Heisman Trophy race and will undoubtedly play a role in determining whether the Hurricanes can stay unbeaten and perhaps knock the Fighting Irish out of the postseason race, Miami still has the edge at the offensive skill positions. That's why our Brandon Marcello picked the nation's top team to beat a 5.5-point spread. Speaking of 5.5-point spreads, Tom Fornelli's Six Pack of picks includes another one with a prediction for No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU. 
Fornelli: "The one thing that would help Alabama's case is if LSU turns the ball over, and we all know Sam Leavitt has that in his bag. But -- But! -- Sam's done a much better job taking care of the football in recent weeks. The return of Trey'Dez Green and emergence of Jackson Harris have helped quite a bit in this department, and Alabama's defense has given up a lot of explosive plays in the passing game this year. The Pick: LSU -5.5 (-110) at FanDuel"We put No. 2 Georgia on upset alert, and the Bulldogs' trip to face No. 10 Ole Miss is among the other games we picked ahead of this colossal Saturday of football.                                                             This week's international game is among the five biggest matchups on Sunday, mostly because it is a dangerous spot for the Bengals against a Falcons team that is similarly in the hunt for a spot in the playoffs. Cincinnati is a three-point favorite, but should it be? Joe Burrow's offense is on upset alert against a defense that gets James Pearce Jr. back from suspension this week. Our Tyler Sullivan would not be surprised if Bijan Robinson bounces back in a big way against a Bengals unit that was just gashed on the ground by the measly Titans. 
Sullivan: "Week 9 presents a great opportunity for Robinson to get back to something closer to the production we saw over the opening month. Entering this international matchup in Madrid, Cincinnati is allowing 122.3 rushing yards per game, which is just outside the top 10 in the NFL. When you dig a bit deeper into the numbers, however, they're even more advantageous for Robinson, with the Bengals allowing 4.8 yards per carry (tied for the fourth-highest in the league)."Don't let last week's scoreless effort fool you; the Falcons continue to play good offensive ball when they are not battling torrential downpours. That's why our Jordan Dajani picked the upset in Madrid. Dajani: "I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. The Week 10 schedule is loaded from top to bottom on Saturday, bringing us one of the most exciting slates in recent memory

        Welcome to one of the most highly anticipated weekends of college football in a long time. With seven ranked matchups on the board, it's going to be an exhilarating frenzy.The day begins with the first-ever top-10 matchup in Holy War history as No. 9 BYU visits No. 3 Utah. The implications of that game are enormous, both in the Big 12 and for the College Football Playoff picture.In the afternoon -- much to the chagrin of Lane Kiffin -- No. 14 LSU will host No. 5 Alabama. After the Crimson Tide were ranked shockingly high in the initial playoff rankings, the Tigers may have a point to prove in Death Valley. The loser will have three losses and playoff hopes on life support.The day will be capped off by No. 1 Miami squaring off against No. 11 Notre Dame. Everyone circled this game before the season, and it hasn't lost any luster. The Hurricanes will be without Malachi Toney, but they can still do the job against South Bend. The Irish, on the other hand, really need to add a quality win to their resume.
Those three games alone are enough for a great Saturday, but there are still four more ranked matchups on the board. These are the types of days we dream about in the doldrums of the offseason.To help you plan your day and prioritize the best matchups, we've compiled a handy viewer's guide.The best gamesNo. 9 BYU at No. 3 Utah -- 12 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): This is in the conversation for the biggest Holy War game ever as the first top-10 matchup in the history of the rivalry. The Utes are undefeated and eyeing a first-round bye in the College Football Playoff. BYU is riding a three-game winning streak against its in-state rival, although the Cougars have underwhelmed in the two weeks since beating Notre Dame. Rice-Eccles Stadium will be a madhouse, and the Utes have never lost at home to BYU as an AP-ranked team. It's just a shame that this is a brunch kickoff locally, but that speaks to the strength of this slate.
No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri -- 12 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): This may not be a playoff eliminator because, theoretically, Texas has a shot to get in with three losses. That said, no one wants to be sitting on three losses in early November. It seems like the Longhorns have gotten back on track lately with consecutive wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Still, those have been costly wins. Texas' Wednesday night availability report featured a litany of key players listed as questionable. Can Missouri take advantage of that and beat Texas through the air with Austin Simmons hitting Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode early and often? That's the Tigers' clearest path to a victory.No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU -- 3:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): First, let's take a moment of silence to mourn LSU missing out on a night game here. Despite all the talk about time slots, LSU has a great shot to win this game with the Sun in the sky. Sam Leavitt has been dealing of late, and Blake Baker's defense could give Keelon Russell some problems. Russell will be the key for Alabama. If the young quarterback can overcome earlier road struggles, he's capable of taking games over. Neither Kalen DeBoer nor Lane Kiffin can afford another loss, but one of them will be 6-3 on Sunday morning.No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio State -- 3:30 p.m. on CBS, CBSSports.com, Paramount+ Premium: This game looks much different than what we expected coming into the season, but the stakes are still incredibly high. Oregon may have gained some confidence with a win over Northwestern, and Ohio State is coming off a disappointing loss in its first game without Julian Sayin. The x-factor in this matchup will be the development of Buckeyes freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who missed a few key throws against USC. If he takes a step forward from one start to the next, Ohio State should be in decent shape, especially with Jeremiah Smith on the outside.
No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 Tennessee -- 6:15 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): Kentucky has been one of the steadiest and most trustworthy teams in college football, but Tennessee has played extremely well at home. The chess match between Will Stein and Jim Knowles will be fascinating to watch, and the Neyland Stadium atmosphere for a "Dark Mode" game will give the Vols' defense an extra edge against the Wildcats. On the other side of the ball, Kentucky's secondary has questions, but sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre hasn't exactly carved anyone up just yet. Maybe that deficiency won't matter for the Cats.No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame -- 7:30 p.m. on NBC, Fubo (try for free): This is one of the most highly anticipated games of the season, even without Malachi Toney on the field. The Heisman Trophy implications in this matchup will be off the charts with CJ Carr squaring off against Darian Mensah. The chances that one of those two produces a Heisman moment are extremely high. It's also a key data point for the College Football Playoff Selection Committee. Neither Notre Dame nor Miami faces a murderer's row this season, so it's a rare opportunity for each side to impress against a quality opponent.No. 2 Georgia at No. 10 Ole Miss -- 7:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): The Georgia defense looked as nasty as ever last weekend against Florida, but it will get a different level of challenge against Trinidad Chambliss in Oxford. Chambliss can elevate everyone else around him, and he'll need to do that to keep the Rebels alive in the College Football Playoff race. If Ole Miss can score points, that will put pressure on Gunner Stockton, who hasn't been sharp in either of his last two outings. If Georgia does have an Achilles heel, it's probably the passing offense.

Malik Nabers has four straight 100-yard receiving games with backup QBs entering Sunday's game vs. Philadelphia
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:44 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        What a difference a few months makes. During the preseason, we were all wondering if Malik Nabers would even be healthy for the start of the season after he had April clean-up surgery following the torn ACL and meniscus injury he suffered in 2025.Now, he looks like a top-five wide receiver who is building off a superb rookie year and poised to carry a rejuvenated Giants team to a division title, with a QB carousel in tow. He put up video game numbers in October:Week 4: 6 catches, 112 yards, touchdown (Jameis Winston at QB)Week 5: 11 catches, 121 yards, touchdown (Jameis Winston at QB)Week 6: 12 catches, 165 yards (Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy at QB)Week 7: 7 catches, 111 yards (J.J. McCarthy at QB)He's the first player with four straight 100-yard receiving games, all with non-Week 1 starting QBs (for the sake of brevity, I'll call them "backups"), since Cris Carter in 1999. It's tied for the longest streak by any player since the 1970 merger, with the likes of Carter, Rob Moore, Jerry Rice and Carl Pickens.That means if he hits the century mark on Sunday vs. Philadelphia, he will be the only player since the merger with five straight 100-yard games with backup quarterbacks. 
Longest streaks with 100+ rec yds, all with backup QBs since 1970QB(s)2026 Malik Nabers4Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy1999 Cris Carter4Jeff George1997 Rob Moore4Jake Plummer1995 Jerry Rice4Elvis Grbac1994 Carl Pickens4Jeff BlakeHe has as many 100-yard receiving games as the rest of the NFL combined with backup QBs this year (four).That's just the tip of the iceberg, too. He's been putting up video game numbers with everyone he's played with since donning a Giants uniform. They used Daniel Jones, Drew Lock and Tommy DeVito in 2024, plus Jaxson Dart, Russell Wilson and Jameis Winston in 2025. All told, Nabers is the only player in NFL history with a 100-yard receiving game with five different starting QBs (Jones, Lock, Wilson, Winston, McCarthy) within his first 30 career games. The only others to hit that mark in their first three seasons were DeAndre Hopkins and George Pickens.Most QB proof since DeAndre Hopkins and Larry FitzgeraldHe's quickly developing the highly sought-after reputation as "QB proof". The gold standard? The aforementioned DeAndre Hopkins and Larry Fitzgerald, of course.Hopkins' legend starts with this fact: He is the only player in NFL history to have a 100-yard receiving game with four different starting QBs in a season. He did this in 2015 with the who's who of backup quarterbacks — Brian Hoyer, Ryan Mallett, T.J. Yates and Brandon Weeden.Hopkins had a 100-yard receiving game with 12 different starting QBs in his career, tied for the most in NFL history. He caught a touchdown from 15 different players, a top-five figure all-time.The OG, though: first-ballot Hall of Famer Larry Fitzgerald. He once had to endure a similar quarterback room of Kevin Kolb, John Skelton, Ryan Lindley and Brian Hoyer in 2012. Oy vey. Fitzgerald caught touchdowns from 16 different players and had 100-yard games from 11 different starting QBs, both top-five ranks all-time. The list of starting QBs both played with is amazing. Forget that Hopkins moonlighted with Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson at the end of his career, and you'll appreciate their greatness more.
                                                                    Microsoft CoPilot
                                                            Here's the list of starting quarterbacks Nabers has played with in 26 career games: Daniel JonesDrew LockJameis WinstonRussell WilsonTommy DeVitoJaxson DartJ.J. McCarthyFellow New Yorker Garrett Wilson might need his QB-proof status revoked if we are comparing him with Nabers.Malik Nabers vs. Garrett Wilson - Tale of TapeNabersWilsonGames2666Rec YPG80.063.2100-yd games811Number of different starting QBs79Top-Five WR status?Time will tell if Nabers is headed for Hopkins and Fitzgerald-level greatness, but he's certainly on the right track. In the meantime, we can appreciate the implications of Nabers ballin' with backups. Division title? Nabers isn't putting up hollow numbers. The Giants are 3-1-1 since Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury, including 2-1-1 during Nabers' historic 100-yard streak. Developing McCarthy? He's helping the Giants get some ROI on the J.J. McCarthy trade. McCarthy is 11-of-14 for 206 yards targeting Nabers in five quarters in a Giants uniform; that's a 2,800-yard pace for an entire season!Top five WR? This offseason, our team of experts ranked the top 10 players at each position and had this as our top five WRs: Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson, Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Amon-Ra St. Brown.As of today, I would edit that consensus list and order it like this:Jaxon Smith-NjigbaJa'Marr ChasePuka NacuaAmon-Ra St. BrownMalik NabersNabers is targeted on 30% of the routes he runs in his career. Only Puka Nacua has a higher rate since 2024. The Giants depend on Nabers so much, and he's delivering, even with backup QBs. CeeDee Lamb, Justin Jefferson, Drake London and co. can duke it out with Nabers for the fifth spot, but I think it's fair to roll with Nabers over his fellow LSU alum Justin Jefferson. It only took Nabers one game to do what Jefferson never accomplished with J.J. McCarthy: have a 100-yard receiving game. CPOY? How about picking up some hardware along the way. Nabers has the second-best odds to win NFL Comeback Player of the Year (+550) behind Patrick Mahomes. It's incredible he's putting up these kinds of numbers with backup quarterbacks when it seemed like he was behind schedule in his recovery from the knee injury he suffered in 2025. 
Massive extension? It all adds up to Nabers being due for a massive extension when he is first eligible for one this offseason. Higgins has always been one of the NFL's best contested-catch receivers, but new dimensions in his game have him producing at a historic pace

        Eight weeks into the NFL season, Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins has been one of the best at his position. Higgins has 43 receptions for 726 yards and four touchdowns, meaning he ranks eighth in receptions, second in yards and eighth in touchdowns despite having already taken his bye week. On a per-game basis, Higgins averages career-bests in receptions (6.1) and yards (10-3.7) per game, putting him on pace for a full-season receiving line of 104 catches for 1,763 yards and 10 scores. Those are marks that have been matched or exceeded just six times in NFL history: by Jerry Rice and Isaac Bruce in 1995, Antonio Brown in 2015, Cooper Kupp in 2021, Tyreek Hill in 2023 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in 2025.Interestingly, Higgins has the exact same number of targets and receptions as teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but he has 234 more receiving yards than his counterpart. It's the per-target efficiency that has been the difference, and it's reversed compared to their previous years together. Higgins' efficiency across many areas is at a career-best level, in fact. He is being targeted on his routes at the second-highest rate of his career. He's converting those targets into yards, first downs and explosive plays at a higher rate than ever. And he's producing successful gain (in terms of expected points before and after the play, according to Tru Media) at a higher rate than ever.
SeasonTarget %Yds/Tgt1D/TgtExpl/TgtSuccess %202021.8%8.4148.1%19.4%53.7%202122.8%9.9248.2%25.5%61.8%202220.3%9.4442.2%22.0%58.7%202319.2%8.6343.4%17.1%53.9%202424.7%8.3644.0%17.4%65.1%202518.7%8.6341.8%21.4%53.1%202624.0%11.9059.0%36.1%68.9%Higgins is doing a lot of the stuff he's always done. He's making contested catches like crazy, using his body to shield defenders away from the ball and haul in the pass that Joe Burrow places for him on a dime. Higgins so far ranks 10th in the league in tight-window receiving yardage despite ranking just 25th in tight-window targets, per NFL Pro. That's because he's caught 60% of the passes thrown in his direction on those plays, the third-best catch rate among the players with 10-plus tight-window targets. (Only Trey McBride and Nico Collins are ahead of him.)
Higgins' average separation on targets this year is only 2.5 yards, per NFL Pro, which is the 10th-lowest mark out of 138 qualified pass-catchers, indicating that Burrow trusts him to win in the tightest of windows.He has been especially effective on back-shoulder throws, which have become a specialty for Higgins over the years. Because he's such a dangerous deep threat, he's able to threaten defenders that he's going straight up the field, then contort his body and reel in the ball when it's thrown just behind him and short of where the defender expects it to go.
But it's not just the usual stuff that has been effective for Higgins. He's expanded the repertoire this season beyond where he's been effective in the past. For example, Higgins has been far more involved in the off-schedule passing game so far this season. He already has more receptions and receiving yards on throws at least 2.5 seconds after the snap than he did all of last year, according to Tru Media, and he's on pace to post by far career-best figures in those areas, as well as nearly all efficiency metrics when it comes to targets on extended dropbacks.
Higgins has also been more involved in the middle-of-the-field passing game than in the past. Because of his role as the X receiver, Higgins has tended to do most of his work outside the numbers, working the deep ball, back shoulder fades, out routes, corner routes, things of that nature. 
But he's running more digs and posts and slants this year, in addition to all the deep and out-breaking stuff, and it's paid off. Higgins has 470 receiving yards on throws between the numbers this season, according to Tru Media, which is already a career high. His 29 receptions on 33 targets on those throws represent an outrageous success rate, as he and Burrow have shown mind-meld chemistry on in-breaking routes so far this season.
Higgins' yards after catch numbers have also bounced back a bit this season after trending downward over the last two years. He's almost a full yard per catch ahead of last season's pace despite the fact that he's seen targets a career-high 13.62 yards down the field, on average, and that the farther downfield players are targeted, they generally produce fewer yards after the catch. Higgins is doing the opposite — creating more yards after catch on deeper-than-average throws.
All of this has resulted in Higgins putting together what looks like a career season. He's been considered over the past few years to be the 1B to Chase's 1A, but their production levels have suggested more that Higgins was the clear No. 2 and Chase the clear No. 1. This season, that hasn't been the case. And the Bengals' offense has been better off for it. Whether that continues through the rest of the season is anybody's guess, but the way Higgins is balling to start the year, I wouldn't necessarily bet against him keeping it up.

        FRISCO, Texas -- Dak Prescott offered a blunt assessment when asked whether the Dallas Cowboys have established an offensive identity through eight games."Is it one we're proud of? I don't know," Prescott said Thursday. "We'll be better, I can promise."Dallas is scoring 27.4 points per game, but its offense has become less varied and less quarterback-friendly in 2026. The Cowboys rank near the bottom of the NFL in pre-snap motion and use play action and under-center formations less frequently than last season.The Cowboys ranked in the top half of the league in play-action rate (28.2%), under-center rate (38.4%) and motion rate (56.6%). With Brian Schottenheimer leading the offensive playcalling, the Cowboys now profile as second-to-last in motion rate (36.5%), 22nd out of 32 teams in under-center rate (30.4%) and 21st in play-action rate. This was always going to be a pass-first offense with Prescott and his superstar receivers, but with general inefficacy (94.1 rushing yards per game, eighth-worst in the NFL) in 2026, Dallas is running the football at the fifth-lowest rate in the league at 32.5%.   
The disconnect is between Schottenheimer and Prescott, with the coach seemingly believing it's harder to use motion when trailing and that it can "cloud the picture" for a quarterback. Prescott has a different approach."Sometimes, it's [motion] just to dress it up and take the defense, give them a different look of us running a core play and breaking some tendencies with a motion to get this play done," Prescott said. "Sometimes it's used strictly for me to see the disguise, to see the matchups that we've got or to create different matchups by moving them from one side to the other and really just getting all the information I can through motion."

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: One realistic, one pipe dream trade scenario for every playoff contender - CBS Sports
description: The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away, and every team is in position to either put themselves over the top in hopes of a playo
body:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away, and every team is in position to either put themselves over the top in hopes of a playoff push, or to completely reset their franchise and move on to NFL Draft season. We've already seen big names like LG Quenton Nelson and DTs DeForest Buckner and Jeffrey Simmons getting dealt before the deadline. And I get the feeling that more big names will be on the move once we get to November 10. For every team in the current playoff picture, we'll break down one realistic trade and one pipe dream trade they can make to put themselves over the top, in addition to a few interesting ones outside of the playoff mix.AFC
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1 . Buffalo BillsPipe Dream Trade: Jessie Bates, S, Atlanta FalconsRealistic Trade: Amani Hooker, S, Tennessee TitansThe Bills have gotten more than enough from their defensive front, a unit that I thought would come along slowly in the beginning of the season. EDGE Greg Rousseau is playing at a DPOY-caliber level, and the emergence of DT Deone Walker has helped their defensive line gain some teeth. However, the Bills have given up the fifth-most completions of 20+ yards in the NFL this season and lack impact play from their secondary. 
Cornerback is a spot where they could improve, but they have a lot of faith in rookie CB Davison Igbinosun opposite Christian Benford. However, the safety spot opposite Cole Bishop could use some improvement. While most people will point to Arizona Cardinals' safety Budda Baker as the top target, he and Bishop's skillsets overlap. Bates is entering the final year of his contract with the Falcons, and he has been an impact player when the ball is in the air and when separating the ball from the player (three PBUs, one INT and three forced fumbles in 2026). Bates is the perfect complement to Bishop and could help tilt the scales back in the Bills' favor. Hooker makes a lot of sense as a realistic target for the Bills. There's some freedom in his contract as he enters the final two years of his 2025 deal, but he's a reliable post safety who can complement Bishop's skills closer to the line of scrimmage.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Denver BroncosPipe Dream Trade: RB Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis ColtsRealistic Trade: TE Dallas Goedert, Philadelphia EaglesI wouldn't be surprised if the Broncos ultimately stand pat at the deadline, after all the rumors and whispers that they're looking for something big. With the emergence of RB Jonah Coleman in this offense, the Denver running game has found some new life to go along with the mandatory second-half Bo Nix resurgence.However, if the Broncos were looking to make a big swing, it would obviously be for Colts' RB Jonathan Taylor. While Coleman has been very good, the explosiveness Taylor would bring makes a pedestrian Broncos offense more dangerous from anywhere on the field (since 2023, Taylor has 78 explosive runs, 5th-most in the NFL). This season, Denver is 26th in Explosive Play Rate, behind teams like the Philadelphia Eagles and the Tennessee Titans, and offense gets really hard when you can't generate explosives. Taylor is not only a big-play machine but would also loosen some of the constraints on the Denver offense as they try to make the Super Bowl.Now, for a realistic trade scenario, I do think the Broncos look at other positions. I doubt they'd be able to get him from within the division, but LB Daiyan Henley could really give the Broncos' defense a nitro boost. However, I'm eyeing Eagles' TE Dallas Goedert as a realistic trade target. 
The Broncos have gotten next to nothing out of their tight end group this year (second-lowest receiving yards to TEs this season, per TruMedia). Goedert is entering the final year of his contract with the Eagles. He would give the Broncos a reliable player down the seams and a competitive blocker who wouldn't be an obvious tell when he's on the field.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Pittsburgh SteelersPipe Dream Trade: WR Josh Downs, Indianapolis ColtsRealistic Trade: CB Amik Robertson, Washington CommandersThe Steelers have surprisingly found themselves at the top of the AFC North behind an offense that's gone fully into bullyball, but at the deadline I think adding a receiver with some separation skills could really give the Pittsburgh passing offense some juice. The Steelers have struggled this season throwing against man coverage, ranking 25th in EPA per play and 30th in Success Rate on all dropbacks against man coverage. DK Metcalf hasn't inspired much confidence in the receiver room, and despite the emergence of rookie Germie Bernard, the room overall doesn't have much teeth.Enter Josh Downs, who is the exact receiver this version of the Steelers needs. Since 2023, among all players with 175 total targets, Downs is 13th in the NFL in percentage of receptions  (80.4%) against man coverage that go for first downs or touchdowns. While he's more of a slot receiver, he's a guy who can win with crafty route running and acceleration in and out of breaks. QB Aaron Rodgers loves throwing sight adjustments and option slants to receivers when he sees the number count in his favor, but those haven't worked with Metcalf. Downs can win on those and give the Steelers an easy button in their passing game.
Their most realistic option could be on the other side of the ball, however. The Steelers' secondary needs more speed and urgency, and no two words embody Amik Robertson more. The Commanders' CB plays with zero fear and has inside/outside versatility, giving DC Patrick Graham options with the cornerback room. Robertson also has experience with Graham from his time in Las Vegas. He feels like an easy and reliable candidate for Pittsburgh to go after.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Jacksonville JaguarsPipe Dream Trade: DT Christian BarmoreRealistic Trade: DT Zach SielerThe Jaguars were in the market for more interior help even before the injury to DT Davon Hamilton, but with Hamilton out for the rest of the season the need for the Jaguars to add there becomes increasingly important. Even with some of the need at safety, Hamilton was a massive part of why the Jaguars were so good in run defense. Losing him puts a significant chunk into what they want to be defensively, and I think the Jaguars will want to replace his spot as they get ready to make a deep playoff run. On top of that, the Jaguars' pass rush production from the interior has been lacking, with rotational DT Ruke Orhorhoro leading the group in pressure rate at 11.2%. Getting more productivity from the group is paramount.There are plenty of names that stand out as trade options at DT, but I think the biggest fish they could get is Barmore, a productive and imposing pass rusher who might be on his way out of New England. The Pats have gotten good play from their rotational guys such as Cory Durden and Leonard Taylor, and while Barmore has been a very good pass rusher, the Pats could see him as expendable. Barmore leads the Patriots in total pressures since 2025, and his 11.8% pressure rate since 2025 would be the best on the Jaguars in that same time period. Barmore's presence would make Jaguars' EDGEs Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker's jobs easier as pass rushers as well.
If they miss out on Barmore, Zach Sieler would be a nice consolation for a cheaper price. The Dolphins are looking more towards 2027, and Sieler doesn't seem to be in the plans for the Dolphins' youth movement going forward. Sieler had a down year last season, but he's a hard charging DT who wins with effort and has 16 pressures in seven games so far. He would take the load off of Hines-Allen and Walker, and while not providing as much pop as Barmore, he would be another quality piece added to the Jags' pass rush.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Kansas City ChiefsPipe Dream Trade: WR Garrett Wilson, New York JetsRealistic Trade: WR Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville JaguarsAre you sensing a theme with the Chiefs? Kansas City has been looking for help since Tyreek Hill left, and this season has been one of the most dire for the receiving group. With WR Tyquan Thornton out for an extended period of time, the Chiefs need more explosive capability and winners against man coverage. Travis Kelce leads the Chiefs in explosive receptions with 10, and Tyquan Thornton is still tied for the lead in that category among the receivers. He's tied with WR Xavier Worthy, but Worthy hasn't proven himself to be reliable downfield or in high-leverage situations. The Chiefs need some more talent in the receiving room and should be aggressive in making a move at the deadline for it.
I'm not sure if the Jets would be willing to part with Wilson, but if there's any pie-in-the-sky trade the Chiefs could make, it would be for Wilson. He's an urgent and explosive route runner who can create separation at all three levels and give the Chiefs an actual legit WR1. He would also allow for the Kansas City offense to slide receivers like Rice and Worthy down the pecking order, where Rice can be a winner on over routes and insert as a Z and movement receiver, while Worthy can be the designer downfield target player. While not on the same level as Garrett Wilson, Brian Thomas Jr. could be a more realistic option for Kansas City if they want to create explosives. The Jaguars seem to want Thomas Jr. around in their offense, but if the right price were offered, Thomas Jr. would give the Chiefs an actual vertical threat in their offense that they won't have with Thornton out. Thomas Jr. sometimes has issues with focus drops and route depth, but he can win outside the numbers on go routes, corners, and out routes, and he has enough size for Mahomes to feel confident throwing the ball to him. Thomas Jr. might not be a WR1, but he would fill a role that the Chiefs desperately need.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Cincinnati BengalsPipe Dream Trade: LB Daiyan Henley, Los Angeles ChargersRealistic Trade: CB Riq Woolen, Philadelphia EaglesWith the Bengals' offense looking like one of the best units in the NFL, the Bengals can start adding more to a defensive unit that has shown really high highs, but also some really catastrophic lows. Cincinnati has spent a lot on the defensive line, and it's paid off (DT Dexter Lawrence is a legitimate DPOY candidate), but the linebacker and secondary rooms could need some major work. The linebacker room especially needs to improve; the unit as a whole has given up the 13th-most yards per coverage snap among all LB groups in the NFL and the seventh-highest positive play rate allowed among all LB groups. In the secondary, star CB DJ Turner is nursing an injury, and Cincinnati could use some more juice from the cornerback room to allow CB Dax Hill to play nickel, where he's at his best.To address the LB position, Henley would be a hand-in-glove fit for what the Bengals are looking for. The Chargers might not be in the mood to sell anyone, but with Henley not yet getting an extension from LA, it could be time for both to part ways. Henley is an urgent player who can fix the Bengals' gaps in pass coverage and thrive as a blitzer, getting downhill to make plays. In Al Golden's defense, he'll provide an immediate upgrade to the linebacker group the Bengals are trotting out right now.
Woolen is a little volatile, but he also would give the Bengals some big-play capability at cornerback and the ability to move Hill back inside to the slot. He hasn't been his best this season in Philadelphia, but in a defense that allows him to exclusively play the vertical plane, he could get back to top form.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. New England PatriotsPipe Dream Trade: EDGE Alex Highsmith, Pittsburgh SteelersRealistic Trade: EDGE Will McDonald IV, New York JetsThe Patriots find themselves in a really fascinating situation, where most of their impact players are injured, but could be back before the playoffs. Left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker is going to be back this season after being put on IR, as will WR AJ Brown. Maybe a trade for another offensive lineman like Eagles' guard Landon Dickerson would help this offense (Vera-Tucker moves to right guard in this scenario), but reshuffling the deck chairs like that could cause a lot of crossed wires. Defensively, however, the Patriots could stand to add some different types of players to their pass rush room. EDGE Elijah Ponder has been a revelation, and rookie Gabe Jacas as well as free agent addition Dre'Mont Jones have added more physicality to the room. However, they could add some more players with speed and burst to the building. Harold Landry III hasn't played, and head coach Mike Vrabel hasn't given any clear return date, meaning it's more likely than not that Landry will not play this season. Adding a speed-based pass rusher to the room could allow for the Pats to vary up their approaches and keep offenses guessing.
The Steelers also have a fascinating problem on their hands. While they do sit at the top of the division, they have three highly paid EDGE rushers who can't all play together. Looking across the board, Highsmith's contract is the most tradeable, and he could recoup some nice value for the Steelers. Highsmith is the exact type of player New England needs, explosive upfield with a variety of ways to get to the QB, including a wicked spin move. It'll cost a little bit more than expected, but Highsmith would give the Patriots EDGE room some much-needed juice.Lower down the totem pole, Jets' EDGE Will McDonald IV looms as a trade target. Another guy who wins with speed and inside counter moves, he's seen his snap count decrease with the additions of Joseph Ossai and David Bailey. In-division trades are rare, but not unheard of, and with McDonald still looking for an extension, some new scenery in New England could be helpful.NFC
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1 . San Francisco 49ersPipe Dream Trade: WR Josh Downs, Indianapolis ColtsRealistic Trade: WR Calvin Ridley, Tennessee TitansDowns pops up again as an ideal trade candidate, but this time we flip conferences and go to the current NFC No. 1 seed in San Francisco. The Niners' WR room looks like a graveyard right now, with WRs Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson all popping up on the injury report. If none of those guys are 100%, you're looking at a WR group of Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks. Not exactly inspiring if you want to go win a Super Bowl. Downs' ability to win with his route running and burst from the slot would give the Niners another option against man coverage and complements Evans really well when they'd both be on the field. Adding Downs helps round out the room and gives the Niners another option in a loaded offense, especially once everyone is healthy.Calvin Ridley is a bit of a fascinating trade candidate at this point of his career. He's clearly not what he once was and has also been nursing an injury himself, but the hope is that a change of scenery gets the most out of him. He can win underneath and still has veteran savvy to help him get open.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Minnesota VikingsPipe Dream Trade: RB Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis ColtsRealistic Trade: RB Tony Pollard, Tennessee TitansThe Vikings should be in the market for a running back at the deadline, whether it be a big splash or a smaller addition. Lost amidst the Kyler Murray disappointment talk is the fact that the Vikings can't run the ball consistently at all. Minnesota sits at 25th in EPA per play on all designed RB runs and 28th in rushing success rate on RB runs. On top of that, the Vikings' RBs don't make anyone miss; they sit tied with the Raiders for last in the NFL in avoided tackle rate, per TruMedia. Part of that is the injuries to LG Donovan Jackson and TE Josh Oliver tanking the run game, but their running backs can't stay healthy either. Aaron Jones is more of a specialty third-down back at this stage, and Jordan Mason just came off of IR. Getting someone to take the lead in that room is huge for that offense.Of all the Jonathan Taylor landing spots, Minnesota is the one I hope happens the most. This feels like the cleanest fit in terms of need, and Taylor combines the best of Mason and Jones as a runner. Getting Taylor's explosive capability and ability to make people miss would make the offense feel less congested, and maybe take some pressure off Murray.If the Vikings miss out on Taylor, Tony Pollard wouldn't be a bad consolation prize. Pollard is playing some of his best ball this season, showing nice finishing ability on his runs along with his already impressive explosive capability. He can also be a factor in the receiving game, reducing how often you need to put Aaron Jones in.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. New York GiantsPipe Dream Trade: RB Breece Hall, New York JetsRealistic Trade: DT Grover Stewart, Indianapolis ColtsIt's no secret that the Giants are looking for a running back. Najee Harris is gone, and Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy haven't inspired much confidence. The Giants currently sitting at 30th in success rate on all designed RB runs and 28th in explosive run rate. In an offense without a QB, having a run game that doesn't constantly put them behind the eight ball could give the Giants much more teeth as we enter the playoff push part of the season.While I don't think a trade for Taylor makes sense for this team, I could see a move for Breece Hall if the Jets are willing to move on him. Hall has had issues staying healthy, but he's a big play machine who wins with burst and acceleration through lanes. He would make an offensive line that's played well shine even more while making offense just feel much easier for the QB.However, a more realistic (and still very good) trade for the Giants would be a move for defensive tackle. The Giants have given up the eighth-highest EPA per carry on runs between the tackles, according to NFL Pro, and their 4.8 yards per carry allowed between the tackles is third-highest this season. Adding a veteran defensive tackle like Grover Stewart would immediately raise the floor of that run defense, with his ability to clog lanes giving LBs Arvell Reese and Tremaine Edmunds more chances to make plays in a completely clean run.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Carolina PanthersPipe Dream Trade: EDGE Khalil Mack, Los Angeles ChargersRealistic Trade: CB Donte Jackson, Los Angeles ChargersThe Panthers should be blowing the Chargers' phone up right now. Despite leading the NFC South, Carolina has taken two major hits to their playoff chances after getting physically overwhelmed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers. While their biggest issue probably isn't getting fixed with a trade at the deadline (offensive tackle), they can still try to revamp a defense that's been decimated by injury. That's where the Chargers come in. If LA were to sell, the Panthers would be smart to go and pry some of their defenders away in hopes of making a playoff push.Khalil Mack makes too much sense for the Panthers. I think his Chargers teammate Tuli Tuipulotu gets an extension from LA that keeps him around, but Mack is still a quality pass rusher and sets a physical edge. The Panthers' EDGE depth has been decimated by injury all season, but adding Mack would give them another veteran presence and more physical play.If we move to the back end, where CBs Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are injured, I think adding a veteran corner like Donte Jackson would make a ton of sense, too. He's played in a lot of schemes and is smart in zone coverage, which is what the Panthers major in. He also has experience playing inside and outside, which would give the Panthers plenty of options once Horn and Jackson potentially return to the starting defense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Chicago BearsPipe Dream Trade: EDGE Khalil Mack, Los Angeles ChargersRealistic Trade: CB Amik Robertson, Washington CommandersA potential Khalil Mack return to Chicago would be a trade I'd be super excited for. The Bears did just trade for an impact player in DT Jeffrey Simmons, but adding another guy to that defensive line to help everyone fit a little better into their roles would help take the defense to a new level. Montez Sweat had his best game this season in their Monday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, and Austin Booker has had more consistent flashes as a pass rusher, but getting a guy who sets a solid edge to rotate with Booker could be helpful. Mack coming back to Chicago would be a great story, but he would also round out the EDGE room in a big way.A trade for a cornerback feels more likely, with CB Jaylon Johnson struggling and CB Tyrique Stevenson being more of a backup. Finding an outside corner would be paramount here, so a guy like the Titans' Alontae Taylor feels a bit out of the picture. Dolphins' CB JuJu Brents feels like a possibility, but Commanders' CB Amik Robertson feels like a guy that would fit on the outside opposite Johnson. He's aggressive and can disrupt receivers despite being undersized. He's played in man and zone concepts, but in Dennis Allen's defense, they can really turn him loose.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Detroit LionsPipe Dream Trade: CB Charvarius Ward, Indianapolis ColtsRealistic Trade: CB Amik Robertson, Washington CommandersIf you're reading this, the Lions still might need you to play cornerback. Their secondary has been the weakest part of the defense this season by a massive amount. Even though they got S Brian Branch back (and S Kerby Joseph has returned to practice), adding more cornerbacks to a room devastated by injury and poor play could help this defensive line transform from being very bad to at least passable for a playoff team.The Colts' fire sale isn't limiting anyone, and Ward could be a player that the Lions add to give them needed experience in man coverage and production on the outside opposite DJ Reed. Ward has been in and out of the lineup since coming to Indy, but when he's healthy, he can still produce as an outside corner. If the Colts don't feel like selling Ward, a reunion with Amik Robertson would make a lot of sense for both sides. Robertson knows the defense, can play inside and out and is a fan favorite. Bringing him back has to be considered in Detroit.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Green Bay PackersPipe Dream Trade: OG Landon Dickerson, Philadelphia EaglesRealistic Trade: RB Tyjae Spears, Tennessee TitansFor the Packers, the biggest addition they'll get is actually coming from inside the house. EDGE Micah Parsons is coming back to practice, adding one of the three best EDGE defenders in the NFL to the lineup. Once he gets back up to speed, the Green Bay defense should be dangerous. However, the Packers' run game is simply mortifying. On all RB runs this season, Green Bay is 29th in explosive run rate and success rate, last in EPA per carry and 31st in yards before contact per carry. Giving this run game some life has to be the top priority at the deadline, and there are a couple of ways Green Bay can go about that.The pie-in-the-sky dream would be to trade for Eagles guard Landon Dickerson. While Dickerson has dealt with injuries for the last two seasons, his physicality and productivity would help pry open run lanes for the Packers' rushing offense. Laken Tomlinson has played well after being a street free agent signing for Green Bay, but the spot at left guard has been a revolving door between Aaron Banks and Donovan Jennings, and nothing behind either door has been good. Adding Dickerson could help lift that run game in a big way.If they can't swing a deal for Dickerson, adding an explosive back like Spears to the room could be really fun. Green Bay has six explosive runs this season and is behind the Miami Dolphins in tackle vvoided rate. Spears would give the room some much-needed juice and capability on third down as a receiver and pass blocker.Contenders just outside the picture
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle SeahawksPipe Dream Trade: EDGE Yaya Diaby, Tampa Bay BuccaneersRealistic Trade: WR Josh Downs, Indianapolis ColtsVery quietly for the Seahawks, their EDGE depth has been rampaged by injury. EDGE Uchenna Nwosu missed the Monday night loss to the Bears with an ankle injury, and EDGE Dante Fowler has been subpar in his time with the Seahawks. Adding to the EDGE room might be a bit of a luxury given the state of the offense, but if they could swing for a guy like Diaby from the Bucs, it would round out that room in a big way. Diaby plays with power and length, fitting the archetype of Mike Macdonald edges. Swinging a move for Diaby would allow the Seahawks to have a hockey lines situation of pass rushers waiting to make plays, much like their run to the Super Bowl last season. Then, if they want to get younger in the offseason, they can extend Diaby.On the offensive side, finding someone that isn't all-world receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba to produce at receiver has been a big issue. WR Tory Horton has been in and out of the lineup with injuries, Cooper Kupp has been more of a dirty-work receiver at this point and Rashid Shaheed has been virtually nonexistent. Downs would give the Seahawks another separator who can win against multiple coverages, making offense feel a little less stressful.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles RamsPipe Dream Trade: WR Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville JaguarsRealistic Trade: CB Donte Jackson, Los Angeles ChargersOn the surface, the Rams' offense feels like they haven't really missed a beat. They're third in success rate, ninth in EPA per play and 10th in points per drive. However, their explosive play rate has dropped from 12.6% last year to 10.4% this year, and their explosive pass rate has dropped from 18.6% to 11.2%, a drastic falloff. If the Rams are going to be without WR Davante Adams and TE Terrance Ferguson for the extent of this playoff push, the explosive plays in this offense are nonexistent. The Rams need someone to take the top off the defense consistently to open up underneath areas for WR Puka Nacua and the run game to thrive.Brian Thomas Jr. would give the Rams some big-play ability in their offense. The Jaguars might not be keen on trading him at this point, but for the right price, I think they would entertain the idea. Thomas has been losing playing time in Jacksonville, but in Los Angeles he could be the stick of dynamite the Rams need while Adams and Ferguson are on IR.On the flip side, the Rams' defense has been decimated by injury. While they get EDGE Myles Garrett back soon, CB Jaylen Watson is going to be out for the season with a shoulder injury. That leaves CB Trent McDuffie with…Emmanuel Forbes Jr and Josh Wallace at cornerback. For a team that wants to play multiple DBs on the field on money downs, going and getting another cornerback has to take priority. Jackson feels like the veteran presence the Rams normally go for in the secondary, with the ability to play multiple roles and thrive in off-coverage.

title: UConn vs. Michigan prediction, pick, odds, spread: Dan Hurley eyes National Championship game revenge - CBS Sports
description: The Michigan-UConn heavyweight tilt features loaded backcourts and high-dollar transfer bigs. Here's what you nee
body:
The Michigan-UConn heavyweight tilt features loaded backcourts and high-dollar transfer bigs. Here's what you need to know
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        You don't have to dig deep into the archives to hype this game up. It's the rematch of the 2026 National Championship game. Dusty May and the always-quotable Yaxel Lendeborg aren't around anymore, but the star power isn't hard to find. Michigan believes it has the best backcourt in college basketball. Get this: UConn also believes it has the best backcourt in the sport.What more could you possibly want?Let's dive into the matchups to watch ahead of this big-boy brawl, starting with the projected starting lineups for each side:Michigan: G Elliot Cadeau, G Trey McKenney, G Roddy Gayle Jr., F JP Estrella and C Moustapha ThiamUConn: G Silas Demary Jr., G Braylon Mullins, G Jayden Ross, F Nik Khamenia and C Na'jai Hines
UConn vs. Michigan: Need to knowBest on best: Cadeau and Demary Jr. are both front-runners for the Bob Cousy Award, given to the best point guard in America. Cadeau is a wizard playmaker who mixes speed, power and creativity. In an ideal world, Cadeau would love to finish a game with 12 assists rather than 20 points, but new Michigan head coach Mike Boynton Jr. may need him to score more than ever before. That's easier said than done because Demary is an elite point-of-attack defender. Demary is all of 6-foot-5 who takes it personally if anyone works him for a bucket. The team with the best point guard play will win this game, but it's as close to a draw on paper.Portal bigs: UConn and Michigan had to replace a combined five NBA players who all played in the frontcourt. UConn spent big in the portal for Seton Hall transfer Na'jai Hines, who is a total freak. Michigan did the same with Cincinnati transfer Moustapha Thiam, who is expected to suit up in this one after missing the opener against Oakland with an illness. Bigs from the portal always take a little time to fully coalesce for their new teams, but UConn and Michigan don't have time to wait. Thiam and Hines need to be immediate difference-makers. Specifically, keep an eye on when UConn aggressively hard-hedges Michigan's ball screens. Hines can be a bit foul-prone when he's flying out to try and be disruptive. Those avoidable fouls drove Dan Hurley up a wall in the preseason and earned Hines plenty of time on the pine. Conversely, that coverage forces the ball out of Cadeau's hands and into Thiam's hands. The 7-foot-2 big fella has to make good decisions if Michigan wants to find good shots, but he's not a great passer (yet). Friday's test should be enlightening on both sides of the aisle.
Preseason hints: Some over-index on preseason results. Others completely ignore them. The truth is likely more in the middle. In the preseason, UConn's defense looked way ahead of schedule. It put Purdue in clamps for long stretches. Hurley has grown men, positional size and at least one elite defender at every single level. Meanwhile, Michigan doesn't look super connected on defense yet. We already knew Michigan's defense was not going to be on the level of the 2025-26 squad's special group. The question is whether this UM squad is a top-25 or top-50 unit. Any disconnected defense is going to be in hell against the labyrinth that is the UConn offense.Where to watch UConn vs. Michigan liveDate: Friday, November 6 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: TD Garden -- Boston, MATV: TNT | Stream: Fubo (try for free)UConn vs. Michigan prediction, picksThe starting 5s for each of these teams are pretty even. Cadeau and Demary are a draw at point guard. Snipers like Trey McKenney and Braylon Mullins are pretty similar. On and on we go. The difference is the bench. UConn can bring a potential first-round pick off the bench in linebacker Colben Landrew. Michigan planned to have something similar, but five-star freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. blew out his knee on the Wolverines' international tour. UConn is the deeper team and looks ahead of schedule on both ends of the floor. Michigan's defense isn't airtight, and I also struggle to envision how the Wolverines create good shots if Cadeau ever gets into foul trouble. 
This line opened with UConn as a three-point favorite and understandably got hammered. It's ballooned out to six. But two whole possessions feels a bit rich for a game where the top-shelf talent is basically even on both sides. UConn can out-physical a lot of teams, but not Michigan. Gayle, Cadeau and McKenney are physical guards. Plus, if Hines gets in foul trouble, I'm not quite convinced Oskar Giltay is ready to be a needle-mover against a talented frontcourt like Michigan's. UConn ain't losing in Boston, but the points are the right side here at anything north of six.
